rationale:
## What changed

Rewrote only the top-level `sc-pipelines` router's YAML `description` (the one thing the
agent sees before deciding whether to open the skill at all; nested per-pipeline SKILL.md
files are never separately listed, so this is the single lever for every task in this
skill). Left every pipeline's own SKILL.md body untouched.

The new description (1) names a few more generic method keywords that tasks actually use
-- rank_genes_groups, Wilcoxon, Spearman, Pearson, consensus NMF, cNMF, mashr, variance
partitioning -- alongside the existing pipeline names, and (2) adds one explicit clause:
fire even when the task already spells out its own step-by-step method, and check for a
fixed script before writing one by hand.

## Why

wiki/REGRESSIONS.md flags "programs" (gene-program and cNMF discovery) as a train
regression: noskill passed 2/2, v1 passed only 1/2. Per wiki/programs/observations.md and
hypothesis.md (tag description-fixable), the router never loaded in either v1 run, so both
agents hand-wrote the full cNMF pipeline from scratch, and one burned all its turns on that
before finishing -- a failure mode the ready-made gene_programs.py script would have
avoided. I confirmed from the rep_1 transcript that the agent never touched the skills
directory except for one incidental "ls -la" listing right at the very end of the
(truncated) run -- it never opened the router at all -- and confirmed in the gene-programs
pipeline's own SKILL.md that the script's fixed defaults (density-threshold 2 keeps all
components, median-of-cluster consensus, per-replicate seeding from a seed flag) already
match this task's explicit spec, so loading the skill would have produced the right answer
quickly. The miss isn't a keyword gap -- "gene programs" was already in the old description
-- it's that the task read as fully self-specified, and the agent chose to just implement
it rather than open the skill. The same pattern (never loaded, but happened to pass anyway
via the model's own knowledge) shows up for "grouptest" and "markers". The new closing
clause targets exactly that trigger-avoidance pattern, and the added method keywords match
vocabulary the earlier description lacked at the router level even though it already
existed deeper in the per-pipeline tables.

The other flagged regression, "signature", is tagged not-skill-fixable in
wiki/signature/hypothesis.md: the failing run's skill script already produced the correct
answer, and the loss came from an unrelated post-hoc edit loop (fighting a hook) that ate
the remaining turns before answer.md was written. No skill-side lever exists for that, so I
left it alone per the instructions on not-skill-fixable gaps.

I did not touch any pipeline's body: "annotate", "ccc", "embed", "mofa", and "tfact" all
show the skill loading and the fixed CLI and body contract working correctly when it does,
which is evidence the bodies are fine as written.
